title: One model list: ModelChoice is the only selectable model; GraphChoice folds in and collection members become ModelChoices (DSL members allowed)
description:
Every ModelScene (mesh node viewer, embedded T-mesh, dungeon viewer) shows one menu, SceneModelMenu, but the list behind it is stitched from three representations of 'a model':
- ModelChoice in a ModelCatalog: display name, path, Kind (MESH_FILE, DSL, COLLECTION), scanned from directories (the mesh viewer's repo .dsl files and staging).
- GraphChoice: display name, .dsl path and its own overrides map, registered in code by a scene (registerGraph: dungeon, T-mesh); availableModels() converts each to a ModelChoice with a 'graph:' token marked MESH_FILE.
- ModelCollection: parallel arrays (names, paths, settings, keep flags, counts) scanned from a directory of scans, mesh files only (MeshLoader.isSupported); while open it replaces the catalog through SceneCollectionMenu.
So a DSL model has two representations, a collection cannot hold a DSL, and overrides exist twice (each GraphChoice's map and ModelScene.overrides, merged on every run at ModelScene.java:369).

Make ModelChoice the only selectable-model class: a registered graph is a ModelChoice of kind DSL carrying its literal overrides (GraphChoice goes); a collection's members are ModelChoices, so .dsl files can be members; a single model opened alone is a one-member collection. The collection then holds the requested model and the scene's overrides (which survive model switches and exist before the first run), which settles ENG-37's MODEL question: the MODEL subsystem's data is the ModelCollection, not ModelScene fields. No class renames.
definition-of-done:
1. GraphChoice is gone; scenes register their graphs as ModelChoice entries of kind DSL with their overrides.
2. ModelCollection members are ModelChoices; a .dsl file in a scanned directory is a member and loads like one; the collection.dsl manifest still records membership and keep/reject (existing manifests still read).
3. A model opened on its own is a one-member collection; ModelScene.overrides moves onto the collection and still survives model switches and can be set before the first run (ixdar-cli model --set, terminal set).
4. The model menu, cn next/prev, ml, the collection-* CLI routes and switch-model behave as before in mesh-viewer, the T-mesh scene and the dungeon viewer.
5. Tests for DSL members, registered graphs with overrides, and overrides surviving a switch; mvn test and test_cli pass.
6. Launch entries and screenshots.
testing-plan:
1. Before any change, record collection-list, ui-state model lists and a model switch with an override set, in mesh-viewer, the T-mesh scene and the dungeon viewer; compare after.
2. mvn test; uv run python -m unittest ixdar_automation_cli.test_cli.
changes-made: GraphChoice is gone: ModelChoice carries a graph's literal overrides, and the T-mesh and dungeon scenes register their graphs as ModelChoices of kind DSL. ModelCollection members are ModelChoices (a .dsl file beside the scans is a graph member, the collection.dsl aside) and the collection holds the overrides; a model opened alone is a one-member collection with no manifest (ModelCollection.open carries the overrides across switches). ModelScene.overrides, currentChoice, GRAPH_PREFIX and the graph: token are gone; requests carry the ModelChoice and loads dispatch on its kind. Collection-only behaviour (menu section, cn, ui-state collection, manifest writes) keys on hasManifest(). Python collection_manifest scans .dsl members. Before/after records (tmp/view27/) match except the model route's path for a registered graph (now its resource path instead of graph:<name>) and a new kind field on ui-state collection members. Tests: ModelCollectionTest (DSL members, old manifest reads back byte-identical, overrides carried across switches), RegisteredGraphTest; mvn test 567/0, test_cli 104/0.
review-summary: ModelChoice is now the only selectable-model class: scenes register graphs as ModelChoices with their overrides, ModelCollection holds ModelChoice members (.dsl graphs included) plus the overrides, and a model opened alone is a one-member collection. This gives terminal commands one data object for the model a scene shows.
